declarations.name: Causal.Causality.iUnion_Iminus_eq_of_dual_pastInextensible
declarations.notes: This is the exact converse of dual_iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_futureInextensible (:330), checked mechanically. A stdin metaprogram opens the twin's four implicit binders [M, inst, C, W] and instantiates (a)'s type at the same fvars. It finds (a).hyp == twin.concl: true and (a).concl == twin.hyp: true, as syntactic Expr equality. So the same W and the same curve classes appear: C.FutureInextensible W / C.dual.PastInextensible W, each with the same 'chronal on its segments' conjunct ∀ a ∈ I, ∀ b ∈ I, ChronalCurveOn W γ a b, and the same ⋃ t ∈ I, Iminus/Iplus W {γ t} = ↑W. There is no extra hypothesis and no separation axiom. Probe.lean's iff example ⟨twin, (a)⟩ typechecks. Its direct constants are dual_pastInextensible_iff, CurveOn.neg and the simp lemmas, as the target says. Non-vacuity: where it is used (in (b)'s proof) the hypothesis is proved by transport from ℝ. Probe.lean also shows the curve class is inhabited: t ↦ exp(−t) over univ is timelikeLine.dual.PastInextensible posHalfLine, and its I⁺_dual union is (0, ∞).

declarations.name: Causal.timelikeLine_posHalfLine_iUnion_Iminus_eq
declarations.notes: Its type equals, syntactically (Expr ==), the domain of the hA binder of GloballyHyperbolic.not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeA. That binder was instantiated at the exact arguments (c) passes: ℝ, PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace, timelikeLine, posHalfLine, t2Space_of_metrizableSpace, timelikeLine_tarentin, timelikeLine_globallyHyperbolic. The proof follows the target's route. Its direct constants include dual_iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_futureInextensible, timelikeLine_iUnion_Iminus_eq_univ, IsSpacetimeExtension.dual, exp_isSpacetimeExtension, IsSpacetimeExtension.iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_pastInextensible, exp_rangeOpens_eq and (a). It is not circular, since (a)'s hypothesis is built by transport and not from (b). Non-vacuity: Probe.lean, recompiled by me with -DwarningAsError=true, proves that Real.exp over univ is timelikeLine.FutureInextensible posHalfLine. It uses LineDevelopment.futureInextensible_of_not_tendsto_atTop, whose CausalCurveIn requires I nonempty, ordConnected and causal on segments. It also proves exp chronal on every segment (timelikeLine_chronalCurveOn_iff: strictly monotone, continuous, positive). It then instantiates (b) to get ⋃ t, I⁻(exp t, (0, ∞)) = (0, ∞). So the curve class of (A⁻) on (0, ∞) is inhabited by a genuine future-inextensible chronal curve. The only hypotheses are the (A⁻) curve-class membership. No metric, curve length or geodesic appears; the ℝ topology instance is the standard one, as in the existing witnesses.

declarations.name: Causal.timelikeLine_posHalfLine_not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeA
declarations.notes: It has no hypotheses of its own: ∀ (Ũ : Opens ℝ) (p : ℝ), ¬ timelikeLine.FutureBoundaryChart posHalfLine Ũ p. Its value, read off the olean, is fun Ũ p => GloballyHyperbolic.not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeA timelikeLine_tarentin timelikeLine_globallyHyperbolic timelikeLine_posHalfLine_iUnion_Iminus_eq Ũ p. The head is that theorem, with 10 arguments, and the hA argument is (b) itself. The transitive value closure of (c) does not reach timelikeLine_not_futureBoundaryChart or timelikeLine_not_pastBoundaryChart, so there is no shortcut. It does reach the GH theorem, (b), (a), timelikeLine_iUnion_Iminus_eq_univ, the transport and the twin. The REPORT discloses that, like the other timelike-line witnesses, this shows the hypotheses jointly satisfiable, not FutureBoundaryChart inhabited. The docstrings say it agrees with timelikeLine_not_futureBoundaryChart, which is true. The statement shape matches its twins at :550 and :572.
